evals.prompt: /team-review 482 — this PR touches our payment processing and adds a new auth middleware, want a thorough review before we merge
assertions: Ingests the PR via gh pr view/gh pr diff (or equivalent) rather than guessing at the changes
Runs a Phase 1 project discovery step before spawning reviewers
Given the security-sensitive scope (payments, auth), selects full mode (7 reviewers) without asking, per the plain triggers in the skill
Spawns reviewers as named agents via the Task tool and never references a 'Teammate' tool, 'spawnTeam' operation, or a shutdown_request/shutdown_response handshake
The adversary reviewer's output explicitly engages with (agrees, disagrees, or adjusts) at least one other reviewer's finding rather than only listing independent findings
Produces a single consolidated report with severity-classified findings (Critical/Major/Minor/Nit), each grounded in a real file:line the reviewer read
Does not edit any code, run tests, or commit changes

evals.prompt: /team-review 91 — small PR, 3 files, but one of them touches the login token refresh logic
assertions: Recognizes the signals are mixed (small file count but touches auth) rather than silently defaulting to either mode
Uses AskUserQuestion (or states it would, if AskUserQuestion is unavailable) to ask the user to choose full vs lite mode instead of guessing
The question presents both options with their real tradeoff (agent count / cost vs thoroughness), not a vague yes/no
Does not spawn any reviewer agents, run gh/git ingestion for a full review, or produce a findings report before the mode question is resolved
Does not fabricate or assume a scoring formula (no point totals) — reasoning is stated in the plain-language trigger terms from the skill, not arithmetic

evals.prompt: /team-review 200 — please review this PR, but Task/subagent tools aren't available in this environment right now
assertions: Does not attempt to spawn Task subagents or named agents given the stated constraint

Follows the sequential fallback: reads the files in scope itself and works through the checklist dimensions (architecture, security, performance, testing, style, docs/UX) one after another as the lead
Performs an explicit self-adversary pass over its own findings (checks for false positives / blind spots) rather than skipping straight to the report
Still produces findings grounded in file:line references from files actually read, with severity levels (Critical/Major/Minor/Nit)
Does not claim to have run 7 parallel agents or reference SendMessage/TaskStop calls that were never made

evals.prompt: /team-review 99999 — review this PR before we merge (this PR number does not exist in the repo)
assertions: Attempts to ingest the PR (gh pr view/diff or equivalent) and detects that the scope is not readable/does not exist
Aborts early and reports the scope is invalid rather than fabricating findings against files that were never read
Does not spawn any reviewer agents (Task calls), run TaskCreate/TaskUpdate for reviewer assignments, or attempt project discovery for a scope that was never confirmed to exist
Does not run any mutating command (no git checkout/reset, no file edits, no commits)
Final message clearly states the PR/commit could not be found and asks the user to confirm the correct number, rather than silently reviewing something else (e.g. --all) as a substitute
